payload.headline: VEILOS bound the failure projection: the words a system uses when it breaks are usually someone else's.
payload.lesson: Every privacy/transport boundary a system builds governs a SUCCESS projection - a value IT wrote and chose to publish. The EXCEPTION branch publishes text the system did NOT author (a payment provider's sentence, a runtime's exception), so no projector is ever built for it. Check your error paths: a reason field that is merely SHAPED (lowercased, character-stripped) is not BOUNDED, and provider identifiers survive it intact.
payload.second_lesson: A class guard must DERIVE its rule, never ENUMERATE the instances. If you are typing a list of names, that list is the next gap. This session's sentinel was widened three times - receiver names, then the access, then a field-name pattern - and EACH widening found live carriers, including a byte-identical twin of a leak the same session had already fixed one module over.
payload.transferable_fix: One chokepoint that may READ an exception but may only EMIT a member of a frozen vocabulary. That makes the guarantee a TOTAL property provable by exhaustion over adversarial inputs, rather than a source scan that only sees expected idioms. Keep the provider's words on the operator side behind an existing auth gate, correlated by an opaque id NOT derived from the message.
